evidence.claim: The report says the prime minister's office concentrates most power and lists unlawful killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, free-expression and assembly restrictions, political-participation limits, and abuses against minorities and women as significant 2022 problems with poor accountability.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The report says the prime minister's office concentrates most power and lists unlawful killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, free-expression and assembly restrictions, political-participation limits, and abuses against minorities and women as significant 2022 problems with poor accountability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government human-rights report summarizing the full year with explicit Bangladesh-specific findings.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional baseline under Hasina's government, not proof of a specific personal order.
contrary_evidence: The report also says civilian authorities maintained effective control over the security forces, which narrows attribution to policy and oversight failures rather than total collapse.

evidence.claim: HRW said opposition groups were reporting escalation of repression, including mass arrests and police raids of opposition homes, and said at least four people reportedly died and hundreds were injured in clashes involving police, BNP supporters, and Awami League supporters after late-August protests.
evidence.title: Bangladesh: Crackdown on Political Opposition
evidence.excerpt: HRW said opposition groups were reporting escalation of repression, including mass arrests and police raids of opposition homes, and said at least four people reportedly died and hundreds were injured in clashes involving police, BNP supporters, and Awami League supporters after late-August protests.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights-organization reporting with concrete event counts and direct attribution questions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Hasina government and its aligned actors as described in the report, though each side disputed blame for the violence.
contrary_evidence: The report notes each side accused the other of instigating violence.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said the clash in Dhaka involved at least one death and more than 60 injuries, that police used live ammunition, pellets, rubber bullets, and tear gas, and that the authorities had launched mass arrests of political activists reaching about 1,400 people.
evidence.title: Bangladesh: Authorities must end repression of demonstrations
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said the clash in Dhaka involved at least one death and more than 60 injuries, that police used live ammunition, pellets, rubber bullets, and tear gas, and that the authorities had launched mass arrests of political activists reaching about 1,400 people.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights-organization statement with specific injury and arrest details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government and police conduct under Hasina's administration; the source does not isolate a single command order.
contrary_evidence: The article is a rights-group response to media reports, not a state audit of every casualty.

evidence.claim: The clashes outside BNP headquarters left one person dead and more than 50 BNP supporters injured, and police then raided the party office and detained several hundred activists.
evidence.title: BNP-police clashes leave one dead as Naya Paltan turns battleground
evidence.excerpt: The clashes outside BNP headquarters left one person dead and more than 50 BNP supporters injured, and police then raided the party office and detained several hundred activists.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting with named event details and arrest counts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The event occurred under Hasina's government and involved police and ruling-party context, though the article also records BNP claims and counterclaims.
contrary_evidence: BNP leaders said police instigated the violence and sought to thwart the rally.

evidence.claim: The Editors' Council said the Digital Security Act was obstructing media freedom and that cases under it had been filed against journalists and other critics including activists, writers, and artists.
evidence.title: Digital Security Act hinders freedom of media: Editor’s Council
evidence.excerpt: The Editors' Council said the Digital Security Act was obstructing media freedom and that cases under it had been filed against journalists and other critics including activists, writers, and artists.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local professional-body criticism reported by a major Bangladeshi outlet; the underlying point is direct but the accessible text is a summary snippet.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The critique is directed at a law used under Hasina's government; it does not by itself prove her personal intent in each case.
contrary_evidence: The government had said it would amend the law, showing some acknowledgment of the criticism.

evidence.claim: HRW said soldiers detained Milon in Dighinala, beat and kicked him for over an hour, took him away in a military vehicle, and that he was later pronounced dead in hospital; HRW said this fit a broader pattern of military abuses in the CHT.
evidence.title: Bangladesh: Indigenous Activist Dies in Military Custody
evidence.excerpt: HRW said soldiers detained Milon in Dighinala, beat and kicked him for over an hour, took him away in a military vehicle, and that he was later pronounced dead in hospital; HRW said this fit a broader pattern of military abuses in the CHT.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed contemporaneous rights reporting with corroborating regional-commission testimony and specific location/time details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Bangladesh military forces under Hasina's government, though the report does not identify a direct PM order.
contrary_evidence: The source is advocacy reporting, but it is corroborated by an independent CHT Commission account.

evidence.claim: Hasina defended the Rapid Action Battalion as a counterterrorism force, questioned the sanctions placed on it, suggested the US should share responsibility because it trained the unit, and said the UN list of disappearance victims was faulty.
evidence.title: Hasina questions sanctions on RAB, wonders if US is unhappy with its counter-terrorism activities
evidence.excerpt: Hasina defended the Rapid Action Battalion as a counterterrorism force, questioned the sanctions placed on it, suggested the US should share responsibility because it trained the unit, and said the UN list of disappearance victims was faulty.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous reporting with clear quotations from the prime minister.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Hasina as prime minister.
contrary_evidence: This is a defense of the force, not proof of accountability or reform; it also conflicts with later rights reporting on reprisals and impunity.

evidence.claim: HRW said Bangladesh intensified restrictions on Rohingya livelihoods, movement, and education, including closing community-led schools, destroying shops, imposing curfews and checkpoint harassment, and keeping many refugees under severe restrictions on Bhasan Char.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Bangladesh intensified restrictions on Rohingya livelihoods, movement, and education, including closing community-led schools, destroying shops, imposing curfews and checkpoint harassment, and keeping many refugees under severe restrictions on Bhasan Char.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual country chapter summarizing 2022 with concrete treatment of a vulnerable group.
evidence.period_fit: covers events of 2022 in a retrospective country chapter
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Bangladesh authorities under Hasina's government, though refugee policy also reflects inherited burden and Myanmar-related constraints.
contrary_evidence: The same section notes a joint repatriation verification plan, showing the government was also pursuing a diplomatic route even though conditions were not safe for return.

evidence.claim: HRW said women in Bangladesh continued to have little recourse to protection, services, or justice in domestic-violence cases, that 193 women and girls were reportedly murdered by husbands or family members in 2022, and that LGBT people faced violence and threats without adequate police protection.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: HRW said women in Bangladesh continued to have little recourse to protection, services, or justice in domestic-violence cases, that 193 women and girls were reportedly murdered by husbands or family members in 2022, and that LGBT people faced violence and threats without adequate police protection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual country chapter summarizing 2022 with concrete vulnerable-group harm indicators and protection gaps.
evidence.period_fit: covers events of 2022 in a retrospective country chapter
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly structural and institutional, but still attributable to the government environment Hasina oversaw.
contrary_evidence: The same section notes a cabinet-approved Evidence Act amendment, showing some partial reform pressure.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that the cabinet approved a draft amendment to section 155(4) of the Evidence Act that removed aspects allowing the defense to denigrate the character of women who pursue sexual-violence charges.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that the cabinet approved a draft amendment to section 155(4) of the Evidence Act that removed aspects allowing the defense to denigrate the character of women who pursue sexual-violence charges.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual country chapter with a concrete legal reform noted in the 2022 period.
evidence.period_fit: covers events of 2022 in a retrospective country chapter
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Hasina-led cabinet as a partial protective reform.
contrary_evidence: This is a narrow procedural reform and does not erase the broader safety and accountability failures described in the same chapter.

evidence.claim: Hasina said she wanted all parties to contest the next parliamentary election and that there was no problem if someone remained in or left the alliance.
evidence.title: Hasina says she wants all parties to contest in next parliamentary election
evidence.excerpt: Hasina said she wanted all parties to contest the next parliamentary election and that there was no problem if someone remained in or left the alliance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous reporting with explicit quotations from the prime minister.
contrary_evidence: The statement is permissive rhetoric, not proof that opposition parties were actually able to operate without retaliation.

evidence.claim: The BNP's Dhaka rally ended peacefully after last-minute permission, even though the surrounding political atmosphere had been tense and earlier clashes and arrests had already occurred.
evidence.title: আন্দোলনের দ্বিতীয় ধাপে বিএনপি
evidence.excerpt: The BNP's Dhaka rally ended peacefully after last-minute permission, even though the surrounding political atmosphere had been tense and earlier clashes and arrests had already occurred.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local-language reporting with a clear description of the rally's eventual peaceful end.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects the broader government-police environment rather than a single named order.
contrary_evidence: The article also says the event came after prior clashes, arrests, and security fears, so it is only partial counterevidence.

evidence.claim: Hasina called BNP and Jamaat a group of murderers and war criminals and urged people to unite so they never returned to power.
evidence.title: PM Hasina urges people to unite against BNP-Jamaat nexus
evidence.excerpt: Hasina called BNP and Jamaat a group of murderers and war criminals and urged people to unite so they never returned to power.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct reporting of the prime minister's public rhetoric, though accessible here as a summary snippet.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Hasina as prime minister and party leader.
contrary_evidence: This is harsh political rhetoric, but it is still rhetoric rather than an explicit call for physical violence.

unresolved_gaps: No direct Hasina-specific 2022 decision on nuclear safety appointments, command-and-control, or emergency doctrine.
No independent audit of Rooppur safety performance or BAERA independence in the target year.
No direct Bangladesh-initiated interstate war, proxy war, or coercive military campaign in 2022.
Direct command-chain evidence for specific 2022 abuses remains thin.
Stronger direct evidence is still needed on institutional restraint, especially courts, election administration, and oversight bodies.
Household-level distribution and independent execution evidence are thinner than macro and program-announcement evidence.
Direct ruler causation for service delivery is thinner than outcome evidence.
Direct first-person evidence of correction, admission, or disclosure is still thin.
The plot-allocation/self-dealing allegations need stronger independent corroboration or final adjudication.
Independent audits of implementation quality and outcome progress are still limited compared with announced-program evidence.
Direct evidence that Hasina personally monitored, corrected, or replaced ineffective implementers is sparse.
